Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Attaching our draft Order Form so your procurement and legal teams have an editable copy. Before we route a formal redline, a few quick clarifying items from commercial/finance that will speed review: 

1) Pricing schedule triggers
   - The draft lists the Tier 2 price kicking in at 1.5M tokens/month. Is Cortexa planning a steady ramp or should we consider a phased trigger (quarterly lookback) for year one?

2) Minimum commit calculation
   - Current language states an "annual minimum" but invoices are monthly. Would you prefer annualized enforcement or quarterly true-ups?

3) Net terms & invoicing entity
   - Redwood prefers Net30 invoicing to Redwood, Inc. If Cortexa requires Net45 or payment to a local EU entity, please confirm the remit entity and the PO workflow.

4) Taxes / VAT handling
   - If Cortexa is EU VAT-registered and reverse-charge applies, we need the VAT ID and a statement on the PO. Otherwise we’ll include VAT on invoices.

5) Attachments & evidence
   - I've included a short SOW line-item spreadsheet to ensure unit definitions match billing.

Could you confirm the preferred answers for items 2–4 so we can propose clean redline language? If helpful, I can book a 30-minute procurement + legal sync later today or tomorrow.

Alex / Tessa / Ben —

Thanks for the quick context. I work with Finance & Ops on invoicing/residency items — a few suggested edits we plan to track in our redline (attached) and a couple asks to close out before final execution: 

1) Minimum commitment language
   - Recommendation: define "Minimum Commit" as an annual dollar amount, with quarterly reconciliation and a true-up invoice (or credit) within 30 days of quarter close. This keeps accountability but avoids a single large true-up at year end. Please confirm Cortexa is comfortable with this mechanic.

2) Net terms / remit entity
   - If Cortexa requires Net45, Redwood can accept Net45 provided the Invoice Remit Entity is Redwood, Inc. and Cortexa supplies a PO referencing our invoice numbers. If Cortexa prefers paying a Cortexa entity, we will need a W-9 / equivalent and acceptance of tax/residency responsibility (Redwood cannot absorb tax gross-ups for third-party remit).

3) Taxes / VAT
   - For EU reverse-charge, procurement must provide VAT ID and an explicit reverse-charge note on the PO. Otherwise Redwood will include VAT on the invoice. If Cortexa requests Redwood to register and remit locally, that will be a scoped professional-services change (we can price that separately).

4) Invoicing cadence & dispute window
   - Proposed invoicing monthly in arrears with a 30-day dispute window; undisputed amounts payable per the Net terms. This is standard and helps cashflow predictability.

I'm attaching a legal redline (high level) and a suggested paragraph for net term exceptions (short clause that ties Net45 acceptance to a PO and valid tax docs). If Cortexa signs off on the quarterly true-up + PO + VAT ID path, we can prepare final execution copy.

Attachments: Cortexa_Legal_Redline_20250825.docx (DOCX, 12KB)
